verses.zh: 巴兰见耶和华喜欢赐福与以色列，就不像前两次去求法术，却面向旷野。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] When Balaam saw that it pleased the Lord to bless Israel,[NOTE:2] he did not go as at the other times[NOTE:3] to seek for omens,[NOTE:4] but he set his face[NOTE:5] toward the wilderness.
notes: For a thorough study of the arrangement of this passage, see E. B. Smick, “A Study of the Structure of the Third Balaam Oracle,” The Law and the Prophets, 242-52. He sees the oracle as having an introductory strophe (vv. 3, 4), followed by two stanzas (vv. 5, 6) that introduce the body (vv. 7b-9b) before the final benediction (v. 9b).
Heb “it was good in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “as time after time.”
The word נְחָשִׁים (nekhashim) means “omens,” or possibly “auguries.” Balaam is not even making a pretense now of looking for such things because they are not going to work. God has overruled them.

The idiom signifies that he had a determination and resolution to look out over where the Israelites were, so that he could appreciate more their presence and use that as the basis for his expressing of the oracle.

verses.zh: 巴兰举目，看见以色列人照着支派居住。　神的灵就临到他身上，
verses.en: When Balaam lifted up his eyes, he saw Israel camped tribe by tribe;[NOTE:1] and the Spirit of God came upon him.
notes: Heb “living according to their tribes.”

verses.zh: 他便题起诗歌说：比珥的儿子巴兰说，眼目闭住（或译：睁开）的人说，
verses.en: Then he uttered this oracle:[NOTE:1] “The oracle[NOTE:2] of Balaam son of Beor,the oracle of the man whose eyes are open,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he took up his oracle and said.”
The word נְאֻם (neʾum) is an “oracle.” It is usually followed by a subjective genitive, indicating the doer of the action. The word could be rendered “says,” but this translations is more specific.
The Greek version reads “the one who sees truly.” The word has been interpreted in both ways, “shut” or “open.”

verses.zh: 得听　神的言语，得见全能者的异象，眼目睁开而仆倒的人说：
verses.en: the oracle of the one who hears the words of God,who sees a vision from the Almighty,although falling flat on the ground[NOTE:1] with eyes open:[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrase “flat on the ground” is supplied in the translation for clarity. The Greek version interprets the line to mean “falling asleep.” It may mean falling into a trance.

The last colon simply has “falling, but opened eyes.” The falling may simply refer to lying prone; and the opened eyes may refer to his receiving a vision. See H. E. Freeman, An Introduction to the Old Testament Prophets, 37-41.

verses.zh: 雅各啊，你的帐棚何等华美！以色列啊，你的帐幕何其华丽！
verses.en: ‘How[NOTE:1] beautiful are your tents, O Jacob,and your dwelling places, O Israel!
notes: Here מָה (mah) has an exclamatory sense: “How!” (see Gen 28:17).

verses.zh: 如接连的山谷，如河旁的园子，如耶和华所栽的沉香树，如水边的香柏木。
verses.en: They are like[NOTE:1] valleys[NOTE:2] stretched forth,like gardens by the river’s side,like aloes[NOTE:3] that the Lord has planted,and like cedar trees beside the waters.
notes: Heb “as valleys they spread forth.”
Or “rows of palms.”

The language seems to be more poetic than precise. N. H. Snaith notes that cedars do not grow beside water; he also connects “aloes” to the eaglewood that is more exotic, and capable of giving off an aroma (Leviticus and Numbers [NCB], 298).

verses.zh: 水要从他的桶里流出；种子要撒在多水之处。他的王必超过亚甲；他的国必要振兴。
verses.en: He will pour the water out of his buckets,[NOTE:1] and their descendants will be like abundant[NOTE:2] water;[NOTE:3] their king will be greater than Agag,[NOTE:4] and their kingdom will be exalted.
notes: For this colon the LXX has “a man shall come out of his seed.” Cf. the Syriac Peshitta and Targum.
Heb “many.”
These two lines are difficult, but the general sense is that of irrigation buckets and a well-watered land. The point is that Israel will be prosperous and fruitful.

Many commentators see this as a reference to Agag of 1 Sam 15:32-33, the Amalekite king slain by Samuel, for that is the one we know. But that is by no means clear, for this text does not identify this Agag. If it is that king, then this poem, or this line in this poem, would have to be later, unless one were to try to argue for a specific prophecy. Whoever this Agag is, he is a symbol of power.

verses.zh: 神领他出埃及；他似乎有野牛之力。他要吞吃敌国，折断他们的骨头，用箭射透他们。
verses.en: God brought them out of Egypt.They have, as it were, the strength of a young bull;they will devour hostile people,[NOTE:1] and will break their bones,and will pierce them through with arrows.
notes: Heb “they will devour nations,” their adversaries.

verses.zh: 他蹲如公狮，卧如母狮，谁敢惹他？凡给你祝福的，愿他蒙福；凡咒诅你的，愿他受咒诅。
verses.en: They crouch and lie down like a lion,and as a lioness,[NOTE:1] who can stir him?Blessed is the one who blesses you,and cursed is the one who curses you!’”
notes: On the usage of this word see HALOT 517 s.v. לָבִיא.

verses.zh: 巴勒向巴兰生气，就拍起手来，对巴兰说：「我召你来为我咒诅仇敌，不料，你这三次竟为他们祝福。
verses.en: Then Balak became very angry at Balaam, and he struck his hands together.[NOTE:1] Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and look, you have done nothing but bless[NOTE:2] them these three times!
notes: This is apparently a sign of contempt or derision (see Job 27:23; and Lam 2:15).
The construction is emphatic, using the infinitive absolute with the perfect tense for “bless.”

verses.zh: 如今你快回本地去吧！我想使你得大尊荣，耶和华却阻止你不得尊荣。」
verses.en: So now, go back where you came from![NOTE:1] I said that I would greatly honor you, but now the Lord has stood in the way of your honor.”
notes: Heb “flee to your place.”

verses.zh: 巴兰对巴勒说：「我岂不是对你所差遣到我那里的使者说：
verses.en: Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not also tell your messengers whom you sent to me,

verses.zh: 『巴勒就是将他满屋的金银给我，我也不得越过耶和华的命，凭自己的心意行好行歹。耶和华说甚么，我就要说甚么』？」
verses.en: ‘If Balak would give me his palace full of silver and gold, I cannot go beyond[NOTE:1] the commandment[NOTE:2] of the Lord to do either good or evil of my own will,[NOTE:3] but whatever the Lord tells me I must speak’?
notes: Heb “I am not able to go beyond.”
Heb “mouth.”
Heb “from my heart.”

verses.zh: 「现在我要回本族去。你来，我告诉你这民日后要怎样待你的民。」
verses.en: And now, I am about to go[NOTE:1] back to my own people. Come now, and I will advise you as to what this people will do to your people in future days.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The construction is the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) suffixed followed by the active participle. This is the futur instans use of the participle, to express something that is about to happen: “I am about to go.”
For “in future days,” see the note at Gen 49:1. For more on this expression, see E. Lipiński, “באחרית הימים dans les textes préexiliques,” VT 20 (1970): 445-50.

verses.zh: 他就题起诗歌说：比珥的儿子巴兰说：眼目闭住（或译：睁开）的人说，
verses.en: Then he uttered this oracle:[NOTE:1] “The oracle of Balaam son of Beor,the oracle of the man whose eyes are open,
notes: Heb “and he took up his oracle and said.”

verses.zh: 得听　神的言语，明白至高者的意旨，看见全能者的异象，眼目睁开而仆倒的人说：
verses.en: the oracle of the one who hears the words of God,and who knows the knowledge of the Most High,who sees a vision from the Almighty,although falling flat on the ground with eyes open:

verses.zh: 我看他却不在现时；我望他却不在近日。有星要出于雅各，有杖要兴于以色列，必打破摩押的四角，毁坏扰乱之子。
verses.en: ‘I see him, but not now;I behold him, but not close at hand.[NOTE:1] A star[NOTE:2] will march forth[NOTE:3] out of Jacob,and a scepter[NOTE:4] will rise out of Israel.He will crush the skulls[NOTE:5] of Moab,and the heads[NOTE:6] of all the sons of Sheth.[NOTE:7]
notes: Heb “near.”

This is a figure for a king (see also Isa 14:12) not only in the Bible but in the ancient Near Eastern literature as a whole. The immediate reference of the prophecy seems to be to David, but the eschatological theme goes beyond him. There is to be a connection made between this passage and the sighting of a star in its ascendancy by the magi, who then traveled to Bethlehem to see the one born King of the Jews (Matt 2:2). The expression “son of a star” (Aram Bar Kochba) became a title for a later claimant to kingship, but he was doomed by the Romans in a.d. 135.

The verb is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive; it is equal to the imperfect expressing the future. The verb דָּרַךְ (darakh), related to the noun “way, road,” seems to mean something like “tread on, walk, march.”
The “scepter” is metonymical for a king who will rise to power. NEB strangely rendered this as “comet” to make a parallel with “star.”
The word is literally “corners,” but may refer to the corners of the head, and so “skull.”
The MT reads “shatter, devastate.” Smr reads קֹדְקֹד (qodqod, “head; crown; pate”). Smr follows Jer 48:45 which appears to reflect Num 24:17.

The prophecy begins to be fulfilled when David defeated Moab and Edom and established an empire including them. But the Messianic promise extends far beyond that to the end of the age and the inclusion of these defeated people in the program of the coming King.

verses.zh: 他必得以东为基业，又得仇敌之地西珥为产业；以色列必行事勇敢。
verses.en: Edom will be a possession,Seir,[NOTE:1] his enemy, will also be a possession;but Israel will act valiantly.
notes: Seir is the chief mountain range of Edom (Deut 33:2), and so the reference here is to the general area of Edom.

verses.zh: 有一位出于雅各的，必掌大权；他要除灭城中的余民。
verses.en: A ruler will be established from Jacob;he will destroy the remains of the city.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or, understanding the Hebrew word for “city” as a place name, “of Ir” (cf. NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 巴兰观看亚玛力，就题起诗歌说：亚玛力原为诸国之首，但他终必沉沦。
verses.en: Then Balaam[NOTE:1] looked on Amalek and delivered this oracle:[NOTE:2] “Amalek was the first[NOTE:3] of the nations,but his end will be that he will perish.”
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Balaam) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and he lifted up his oracle and said.” So also in vv. 21, 23.
This probably means that it held first place, or it thought that it was “the first of the nations.” It was not the first, either in order or greatness.

verses.zh: 巴兰观看基尼人，就题起诗歌说：你的住处本是坚固；你的窝巢做在岩穴中。
verses.en: Then he looked on the Kenites and uttered this oracle:“Your dwelling place seems strong, and your nest[NOTE:1] is set on a rocky cliff.
notes: A pun is made on the name Kenite by using the word “your nest” (קִנֶּךָ, qinnekha); the location may be the rocky cliffs overlooking Petra.

verses.zh: 然而基尼必至衰微，直到亚述把你掳去。
verses.en: Nevertheless the Kenite will be consumed.[NOTE:1] How long will Asshur take you away captive?”
notes: Heb “Nevertheless Cain will be wasted; how long will Asshur take you captive?” Cain was believed to be the ancestor of the Kenites. The NAB has “yet destined for burning, even as I watch, are your inhabitants.” Asshur may refer to a north Arabian group of people of Abrahamic stock (Gen 25:3), and not the Assyrian empire.

verses.zh: 巴兰又题起诗歌说：哀哉！　神行这事，谁能得活？
verses.en: Then he uttered this oracle:“O, who will survive when God does this![NOTE:1]
notes: Because there is no parallel line, some have thought that it dropped out (see de Vaulx, Les Nombres, 296).

verses.zh: 必有人乘船从基提界而来，苦害亚述，苦害希伯；他也必至沉沦。
verses.en: Ships will come from the coast of Kittim,[NOTE:1] and will afflict Asshur,[NOTE:2] and will afflict Eber,and he will also perish forever.”[NOTE:3]
notes: The MT is difficult. The Kittim refers normally to Cyprus, or any maritime people to the west. W. F. Albright proposed emending the line to “islands will gather in the north, ships from the distant sea” (“The Oracles of Balaam,” JBL 63 [1944]: 222-23). Some commentators accept that reading as the original state of the text, since the present MT makes little sense.
Or perhaps “Assyria” (so NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT).
Or “it will end in utter destruction.”

verses.zh: 于是巴兰起来，回他本地去；巴勒也回去了。
verses.en: Balaam got up and departed and returned to his home,[NOTE:1] and Balak also went his way.
notes: Heb “place.”
